summary: Tested the new Morts-tab Flock Overview panel + Staff QR flow + standalone /morts-entry page. Backend: 12/12 pytest cases pass (auth gates, push/pull round-trip via farm-token, farm-config auth, idempotent upsert, static page). Frontend: MortsInsightsPanel renders with all 4 KPIs (no NaN/undefined), period selector switches between 7/14/30 days and updates loss-rate KPI, both trend + shed breakdown charts render (recharts SVGs present), Staff QR button opens modal, generates correct /morts-entry?farm=north-creek&t=<token> URL, QR SVG renders, Close button dismisses modal. Standalone /morts-entry with valid token renders all 20 shed cards with Save buttons, farm name loads from /api/farm-config, saving a shed shows the '✓ Saved' badge + toast and POST /api/integrations/morts returns 200.

minor.issue: Accepts ?t=<farmToken> as auth. Since the endpoint's purpose is 'let the logged-in owner fetch the token to build the QR', accepting the token itself as auth is a mild footgun — any staff-QR link recipient could re-fetch the token. Consider requiring an actual session cookie (not _require_farm_access). Not blocking.

integration_issues.issue: Spec says a wrong/missing ?t= should show 'This link has expired or is invalid' from the dark-themed staff page. In production the SPA's auth-guard.js runs before the /api/page/morts-entry fetch completes and, seeing no session AND no valid farm-token, redirects the anonymous visitor to Emergent OAuth (Google sign-in) instead. Result: staff scanning a stale QR see a Google login page rather than the intended 'link expired' message. The static HTML's own error branch (fetch /api/farm-config -> 401 -> show error) is never reached because the guard bounces first.

action_items: Main agent: In /app/backend/static/auth-guard.js, treat /morts-entry as a public no-login page (like a public static route). Either short-circuit the guard when window.location.pathname === '/morts-entry', OR keep the guard but let it accept an anonymous visitor with the URL ?t= present and let the page itself render the 'link expired' error when the token is bad. Otherwise the bad-token UX contract in the spec cannot be met.
(Optional) Harden /api/farm-token to require an actual session cookie (not the farm token) so the QR-link recipient can't re-fetch the master token.
critical_code_review_comments: MortsInsightsPanel is well-scoped and uses shared localStorage state — no data-model coupling issues. Uses recharts consistently with the rest of the app.
external_morts collection: GET returns clean docs (_id excluded via projection) — good.
morts-entry.html is 143 lines, dependency-free vanilla JS, dark-themed to match reader.html palette — appropriately isolated from the SPA bundle.
App.tsx is ~13,584 lines — it is far beyond the 700-line guideline. Not new in this feature but worth flagging: needs modularization.

Backend pytest uses date 2019-01-15 sheds 97/98/99 and cleans up to zeros in an autouse module-scope fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The bad-token /morts-entry UX gap is the only outstanding item — after main agent adjusts auth-guard.js to allow anonymous access to /morts-entry, re-verify by loading /morts-entry?farm=north-creek&t=bad in a fresh (no-cookie) browser context and asserting the 'This link has expired or is invalid' message appears in #content and no redirect to auth.emergentagent.com happens. Regression check the good-path standalone page still loads.
rca of the issue: Root cause: /app/backend/static/auth-guard.js is included by the SPA bootloader (feed-program/index.html) for all app routes including /morts-entry. The guard runs BEFORE the STATIC-page interceptor's document.write can replace the DOM. When there's no session AND the farm token is invalid (backend /api/auth/me returns 401 and any /api/* call with the bad ?t= also 401s), the guard's anonymousBounceUrl() sends anonymous visitors to Emergent OAuth (because /morts-entry has __BBM_PAGE__='app' but is not the homepage exception). The staff HTML's own graceful 'link expired' fallback (lines 135-138 of morts-entry.html) is therefore never reached. Fix: whitelist /morts-entry in auth-guard.js so it returns early without redirecting when pathname === '/morts-entry', trusting the static page to handle bad-token UX itself.
